historic/u3e6/articles-1-5.jpg.description: The Articles of Confederation, pages 1-5: the fear-built government with no tax power.

historic/u3e6/articles-page1.jpg.description: Page one of the Articles of Confederation: one vote per state, no tax power, no executive, no national courts.

historic/u3e6/articles-page2.jpg.description: Page two of the Articles of Confederation, the fear-built government that lasted from 1781 to 1789.

historic/u3e6/fallen-timbers.jpg.description: Fallen Timbers, 1794: Wayne's victory that opened Ohio.

historic/u3e6/hamilton-trumbull.jpg.description: Alexander Hamilton, who used the failed five-state Annapolis Convention of 1786 to call for the Philadelphia meeting of 1787, by John Trumbull.

historic/u3e6/heckewelder-map.jpg.description: Heckewelder's map of the Ohio country: the surveyed townships of the Northwest Ordinance's orderly promise.

historic/u3e6/henry-knox.jpg.description: Henry Knox, whose panicked 1786 letter warned Washington that the rebels saw the government's weakness and felt their own strength.

historic/u3e6/mad-anthony.jpg.description: 'Mad' Anthony Wayne, whose Legion won at Fallen Timbers in 1794.

historic/u3e6/northwest-territory-posses.description: Map of how the United States came into possession of the Northwest Territory, the Confederation's one triumph.

historic/u3e6/old-northwest.jpg.description: The Old Northwest Territory before and after the Ordinance of 1787.

historic/u3e6/royce-ohio.jpg.description: Royce's map of Ohio areas: the Greenville Treaty cessions.

historic/u3e6/shays-fights-back.jpg.description: Depiction of Shays' men in action: the 1781 impost died when Rhode Island alone voted no, and Congress stayed broke.

historic/u3e6/shays-memorial-taunton.jpg.description: The Shays' Rebellion memorial at Taunton, Massachusetts.

historic/u3e6/shays-monument.jpg.description: Monument to Shays' Rebellion, the uprising that terrified the elite into replacing the Articles.

historic/u3e6/shays-rebellion.jpg.description: Depiction of Shays' Rebellion, 1786: debt-crushed Massachusetts farmers shutting the courts and marching on the Springfield arsenal.

historic/u3e6/shays-shattuck-gap.jpg.description: Daniel Shays and Job Shattuck, leaders of the 1786 rebellion, by an unidentified artist, from the Google Art Project.

historic/u3e6/treaty-greenville.jpg.description: The 1795 Treaty of Greenville, ceding most of Ohio after Fallen Timbers.
